annotations.description: Playing Multiversal Passage on turn 1 requires paying 2 life to have it enter untapped, or it enters tapped. Starting Town enters untapped for free on turns 1-3 and can produce any color of mana (at the cost of 1 life per activation for colored mana). Since the player has a turn 2 play (Badgermole Cub at {1}{G} or Explosive Prodigy at {1}{R}), they want untapped mana on both turns. Playing Starting Town first (free untapped) and Multiversal Passage second (paying 2 life for untapped, or accepting tapped if not needed immediately) would save 2 life if they need Multiversal Passage untapped on turn 2, or is equivalent if they pay life for both. More importantly, Starting Town produces any color, which is more flexible on turn 1. Playing Multiversal Passage first means choosing a basic land type now and potentially paying 2 life, when Starting Town would have entered untapped for free.

annotations.betterLine: Play Starting Town first (enters untapped for free on turn 1-3), then play Multiversal Passage on turn 2. This saves 2 life if Multiversal Passage needs to enter untapped, or allows it to enter tapped on a later turn when the tempo loss matters less.

annotations.description: Casting Sleight of Hand before playing a land is a sequencing error. DSV3 Analyst has Multiversal Passage and two Riverpyre Verges in hand. Playing a land first costs nothing and preserves options — Sleight of Hand could reveal information that affects which land to play, but more importantly, playing a land first keeps mana open. Specifically, if they play Multiversal Passage (paying 2 life for untapped) or a Riverpyre Verge, they could have 2 mana available after casting Sleight of Hand, potentially leaving up Spell Snare or Bounce Off. By casting Sleight of Hand first, they use their only mana and can only play a tapped land afterward with no mana open. However, Riverpyre Verge only produces U if you control an Island or Mountain, and Multiversal Passage could be set to Island but costs 2 life. The correct sequencing is to play the land first, then cast Sleight of Hand with the information of what lands you have available, potentially leaving up interaction.

annotations.betterLine: Play Multiversal Passage (choosing Island, paying 2 life for untapped) first, then cast Sleight of Hand off Spirebluff Canal, leaving Multiversal Passage untapped to potentially hold up Spell Snare or Bounce Off. Alternatively, play Riverpyre Verge first and then cast Sleight of Hand, though Riverpyre Verge can't produce U without an Island/Mountain yet.

Bouncing the animated land would set the opponent back a land drop (from 2 lands to 1), essentially acting as both removal and land destruction. The opponent would need to use their next land drop just to replay Multiversal Passage. Meanwhile, the Badgermole Cub can simply be replayed next turn for 1G, and its ETB will earthbend yet another land, potentially gaining even more value than before.

annotations.description: Casting Formidable Speaker on turn 3 is suboptimal compared to Badgermole Cub. Badgermole Cub costs only 2 mana (leaving 1 mana open), creates an additional creature via earthbend, and its mana-doubling ability on tapped creatures synergizes with future plays. Formidable Speaker's ETB requires discarding a card to tutor, which is fine, but the opponent has 2 cards in graveyard (instants/sorceries) and could have Spell Snare ready (counters MV 2 spells) - though both are MV 2 so both are vulnerable. More importantly, Badgermole Cub on turn 2-equivalent mana with earthbend creates board presence and ramp, while Formidable Speaker without a clear discard target is just a 2/4 body. The Speaker is better if you have something worth discarding to tutor for, but the hand has strong cards already. Additionally, casting a creature before combat when holding no combat tricks is a minor sequencing issue but largely irrelevant with no attackers.
